success_patterns: For close options, compare the complete claims, including any added strictness, endpoint, structural condition, or uniform quantitative bound; a single unsupported extra clause can make an otherwise plausible option false.

Use small examples or equality cases to test a precise universal claim, especially when a condition may not guarantee existence or when strict inequality is asserted; treat these as checks, not as substitutes for the general theorem.

patch.reasoning: The current skill already emphasizes literal parsing, quantifiers, endpoint spaces, equality conditions, and examples as checks. These successful trajectories reinforce those rules; a brief addition can make the comparison of nested claims in “strongest statement” questions more explicit without adding theorem-specific facts.

edits.content: For “strongest statement” questions, first check the truth of each option as a whole, then rank the supported claims by logical strength. Separate a base assertion from every added clause: one extra strict inequality, endpoint claim, uniform rate, or structural guarantee can invalidate an otherwise correct option. Do not settle for a weaker true option if a stronger supported one remains.
